howThisDiffersFromTheFirstWave.firstWaveCause: Five of six workers did not know scripts/rcap-corpus/bootstrap-private-corpus.sh existed, searched for an already-mounted tree, correctly found none, and stopped. The dispatch brief was the defect; the bytes were one command away.
howThisDiffersFromTheFirstWave.thisReturnsCause: That defect is fixed and did not recur. The bootstrap was found and run. It failed at the release-resolution step with HTTP 403 from the GitHub API, meaning the credential present in this container cannot read Roger-LegalEase/legalease-source-artifacts. The bytes were NOT one command away here.
howThisDiffersFromTheFirstWave.consequence: This is an access-capability block, not a brief-knowledge block. Re-dispatching this family with a better brief will not resolve it. The container must be granted read access to the source-artifacts repository.

No prior branch existed for this family, so there was no predecessor work to resume. This is a first attempt, not a rebuild.

Resolving Expungement_AI_RCAP_Master_Library_Edition_1.zip from Roger-LegalEase/legalease-source-artifacts@source-corpus-2026-08-28 ... curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 403 / asset not found in release / bootstrap-private-corpus: could not resolve the release asset (the token may lack access to Roger-LegalEase/legalease-source-artifacts)
whatWasAttempted.interpretation: A token IS present in the environment -- the script's own no-token precondition did not trip, and execution reached the API call. The 403 is an authorization failure on the source-artifacts repository, not a missing-credential failure. Nothing was downloaded, nothing was extracted, and the script refused rather than guessing, which is correct behaviour.

whatWasAttempted.detail: The prescribed remedy from the worker brief was called without any preceding curl or git ls-remote probe, exactly as instructed. It was refused by this session's permission classifier, not by GitHub. The refusal is a local policy decision about what this agent may attach, and it is the sole reason the corpus remains unreachable.
whatWasAttempted.notWorkedAround: No alternative route to those bytes was attempted. Reading the release through the GitHub MCP tools would have fetched from a repository that is outside this session's declared scope and whose attachment had just been refused; that is a circumvention of the denial, not a substitute for it. Egress to court and agency hosts is refused by policy and was not attempted either: a copy from anywhere that is not the issuing authority would not be an official source.
